Alptuğ Dağ (b. 2000, Ankara) is an independent film director, creative technologist, editor and voice artist known for his short film Sessiz (2023). He designed and built CineTV from scratch as a free gift to cinema lovers.\n\nFollow @alptugdag on Instagram for upcoming film projects, directing/editing collaborations, or just to say hello.

A minute\'s tour of what this TV can do now. Press OK to go on.
These films are picked for this moment: the hour, the day, your city and the weather. Move left and right; the room lights up in the film\'s colour.
OK on a case: it comes off the shelf and opens, with the story inside the cover and the film\'s trailer playing automatically. OK again: the film starts straight in Nuvio.

Trailer moments are on by default: an opened DVD turns sideways and its trailer plays automatically and muted, with the story across the other side. Switch it off with the Trailer moments tile in Settings.
“car films”, “Nolan films”, “a father whose daughter is kidnapped”, or any question. The shelf fills with the answer.

Press the remote\'s microphone key and talk: a film (“open Inception”), a person (“Kubrick\'s films”), a mood, or a command (“volume down”, “HDMI 2”). Gamze remembers what you just said, so “an older one?” works, and when she asks you something back the microphone opens again by itself.
Press here and scan the code: your phone becomes a touchpad remote that works in every app, with an air mouse, its keyboard typing on the TV, and a real power-off.
In YouTube on any phone, tap Cast and pick this TV: it opens on the TV screen. On the phone page, Cast sends any web video to the TV: playback opens seamlessly.
Your devices by their own names: “PlayStation 5”, “Digiturk”. Live TV is first.
Hold OK (or Menu) on an app to move, hide or uninstall it. The last tile shows every app.

Settings is one scrollable page: themes, visual experience, AI & network, picture-sound-network tuning and system & TV inspector, one under another; arrows at the edges show where you can scroll. Hold the gear for the TV\'s own settings.
After 5 idle minutes, scenes and lines from films fill the screen like a 35 mm reel. The TV sleeps by itself later.

The signature at the top-left belongs to Alptuğ Dağ: press it anytime to meet the creator of CineTV, watch his short film Sessiz, and follow @alptugdag on Instagram to support this free cinema project.
On this TV: not entered yet. Settings › AI & films, or type it from the phone\'s keyboard.
AI key: the brain of the search

Enter an AI key (Gemini is free: aistudio.google.com › Get API key; Claude, OpenAI, Grok or OpenRouter work too) in Settings › AI & films. Without it, search finds titles and people only: no “car films” or “a father whose daughter is kidnapped”, no answers to questions, and no shelf picked for the moment.
TMDB key: posters and Turkish stories

Enter a free TMDB key (themoviedb.org › Settings › API) in Settings › AI & films. Without it, stories come from an English source and are translated, there are fewer posters and backdrops, no director inside the DVD, no searching by people or genres, and Trailer moments cannot play.
Optional: a free MDBList key (mdblist.com › Preferences › API) adds IMDb, Rotten Tomatoes and Letterboxd ratings. Without it, only the TMDB score is shown.
One question to say yes to

If the TV asks “Allow USB debugging?” for CineTV, tick “Always allow” and press OK. That is what makes the phone remote work in every app and keeps CineTV your Home. Leave network debugging on in Developer options.
Once: Settings › Performance › Determine automatically. A short test picks Low, Medium or High for this TV, and each keeps adapting by itself.
AirPods and Bluetooth headphones reconnect to the TV by themselves, and the spatial audio panel (Settings › AirPods) widens the sound for films.
Between 23:00 and 05:00, CineTV activates warm eye-care amber lighting and dynamic whisper audio leveling, ensuring you enjoy cinema without disturbing anyone at home.

While a film plays in Nuvio, YouTube or the player, press the yellow key (or CineSUB on your phone). Rings appear around the people, places, objects, food and art worth knowing, with a note beside each; ◀ ▶ moves between them, OK tells more, Back closes. The film never stops.
Play a test sweep from your phone in your seat; CineTV measures the room and sets the TV\'s equaliser so dialogue stays clear.
Tell her who you watch with, what you loved or hated; she keeps it on this TV only and chooses with it: no violence with the kids around, chemistry for a date, anything goes alone.
Seamless integration with Apple Siri Shortcuts, Google Home and Amazon Alexa: trigger movie night scenes, launch titles or power down by voice.
Lightest. Adapts by itself: fewer films when memory is short, simpler light when graphics struggle

Switch it on in Settings and, every few minutes, CineSUB may float one short note in a quiet corner: a real place, a painting, a name or an event mentioned in the dialogue. It never covers subtitles and fades on its own.

You set the clock. Real stills, portraits and casts from TMDB plus Gamze\'s own questions; everyone answers on their phone, answers open together on the TV, each right one is 10 points. The winner picks tonight\'s film.
Six films in a revolver, one bullet. Take turns on the trigger: an empty chamber knocks its film out, the bullet picks tonight\'s film. The clock shrinks every turn; two spins each.
Cinema taboo with no timer: whoever\'s turn it is picks a film, series or actor the room will know, Gamze forbids five words, and everyone guesses on their phones.
Glass and wood taps for moving around, a low swell when a case opens, a deep hit when a film starts. Interface and game sounds can each be switched off in Settings.
